prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1435; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the claimant's representing attorney, reporting a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection with a wrist fracture to the claimant. Vehicle is drivable but has rear bumper and trunk damage.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force on the date of loss. Coverage verification complete with no issues noted.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. It places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of impact and matches the reported location and general sequence of events.

Entry 4: Photos from the insured and the claimant's side were reviewed. They confirm the rear damage and the approximate point of contact, though no independent witnesses have come forward to describe the collision.

Entry 5: Reviewed the damage against the described impact speed and angle. Most of the rear structural damage is in line with what was reported. A few older scratches on the lower bumper may predate this loss and will be noted separately.

Entry 6: Spoke with the claimant through counsel. The account of how the collision occurred matches the initial statement given at first notice, with no material differences in the sequence or details.

Entry 7: Medical records received. The wrist fracture is consistent with the mechanism of a rear-end impact of this type. No prior injury to the same wrist or arm appears in the claimant's records or in the history provided.

Entry 8: Treatment began within a day of the collision and followed a typical course, including immobilization, orthopedic follow-up, and physical therapy. Treating notes describe steady improvement.

Entry 9: Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage occurred before the coverage start date. The prior-damage question is limited to the few minor scratches already noted.

Entry 10: Sent request to the treating orthopedic provider for updated status and expected recovery timeline. Counsel was copied on the request.

Entry 11: Updated medical report indicates the claimant has progressed well, with therapy visits decreasing in frequency as range of motion returns. Treatment appears to be tapering as expected for this injury.

Entry 12: Reserve reviewed based on the current medical picture and repair estimate. File remains open pending final medical update and resolution of the minor prior-damage note on the bumper.
